title: Scripture Of Love
formattedMarkdown:
# Scripture Of Love

*Inspired by the teachings of Paramahansa Yogananda and Sri Daya Mata of Self-Realization Fellowship*

### The Eternal Language of the Soul

Throughout the ages, humanity has searched for the ultimate truth in sacred books, dogmas, and intellectual philosophies. Yet, the greatest scripture ever written is not one inscribed with ink on parchment, but the "Scripture of Love" written by the Divine Hand upon the very altar of the human heart. Paramahansa Yogananda taught that the entire cosmos was created out of the vibration of God’s love, and it is only through love that the human soul can find its way back to its eternal home in Him.

To understand this scripture, we must go beyond the intellect. The intellect can analyze, categorize, and debate, but it can never touch the hem of the Divine. Only love—pure, unconditional, and selfless—has the power to bridge the gap between the finite human ego and the Infinite Lord. When we open our hearts in deep, silent devotion, we begin to read this inner scripture, realizing that our true nature is not this fragile physical form, but Spirit, whose essence is everlasting bliss.

### The Temple of the Heart

Our beloved Sri Daya Mata, who exemplified this divine love so perfectly during her life, often reminded us that God does not look at our outer accomplishments or intellectual prowess. He looks only at the sincerity of our love for Him. She taught that we must turn our hearts into a temple of peace and silence. In the quiet hours of meditation, we must pray to the Divine Mother, whispering from the depths of our being:

> "Lord, I want nothing but Thee. Cleanse my heart of all desire, that Thy love may flow through me to all of Thy children."

When we empty our minds of the restless anxieties of the world, we create space for the Divine Guest to enter. Paramahansaji taught that God is the most silent and respectful of lovers; He never forces His way into our consciousness. He waits patiently behind the portals of our thoughts, waiting for us to turn our attention away from the distractions of the world and say, "Come to me, Lord. Thou art my only true Friend."

### Transforming Human Love into Divine Love

Human love is often conditional, subject to the whims of expectation, ego, and change. Yet, it is still a reflection, however distorted, of the great Divine Love. Our spiritual task is to purify this human love, stripping away its selfishness, and expanding it until it encompasses all creation. We must learn to see the Divine residing within everyone we meet—not only in those who love us, but also in those who misunderstand or oppose us.

This is not an easy task, but it is the very core of the Scripture of Love. To love those who are difficult to love is the highest form of spiritual discipline. When we do so, we are not acting from the limited resources of our own ego, but we are letting the boundless love of God flow through us. This is the dynamic will in action—the conscious decision to choose love over anger, forgiveness over resentment, and understanding over judgment.

As Paramahansa Yogananda beautifully wrote:

> "To love those who love you is natural; to love those who do not love you is supernatural. It is the love of God that flows through your heart when you can wish only well to those who hurt you."

### The Practice of Unconditional Devotion

To make the Scripture of Love a living reality in our daily lives, we must establish a consistent routine of meditation and devotional practice. Through the scientific techniques of Kriya Yoga, we withdraw our energy from the senses and direct it upward to the higher centers of spiritual perception. Here, in the quiet chamber of the soul, we experience the profound peace and joy of the Divine Presence.

Outside of meditation, we must carry this peace with us into our daily activities. We must practice the presence of God, holding a silent conversation with Him throughout the day. Whether we are working, eating, walking, or resting, we can keep a corner of our minds anchored in His thoughts. In doing so, we turn our ordinary duties into an offering of love to Him.

### Practical Habits for Living the Scripture of Love

To help you weave this divine love into the fabric of your daily life, cultivate these spiritual habits:

* **Begin and End Your Day with God:** Before you engage with the world in the morning, offer your first thoughts to the Divine. At night, before you sleep, place all your cares and anxieties at His feet, asking Him to take charge of your soul.
* **Practice Silent Devotional Whispers:** Throughout the day, repeat a simple prayer of love in your heart, such as "I love Thee, Lord," or "Guide me, Divine Mother."
* **See the Divine in All:** When interacting with others, consciously look past their outer personalities and acknowledge the spark of God within them. Offer a silent mental bow to their souls.
* **Perform Selfless Service:** Seek opportunities to help others without expecting anything in return. Let your hands perform His work and your lips speak His words of comfort.
* **Meditate Deeply Every Day:** Dedicate time each day to go within. Use the techniques taught by the Gurus to quiet the mind and listen to the silent whisper of God's love in your heart.

### A Closing Prayer to the Divine Mother

Let us close our eyes for a moment, sitting tall, with our hands resting on our lap in a receptive posture. Let us take a deep breath, releasing all tension, and offer this prayer from the depths of our hearts:

> "O Divine Mother, Thou art the ocean of love, and we are but tiny waves upon Thy breast. Teach us to submerge our small egos into the vastness of Thy love. Write Thy scripture of love upon our hearts, that we may read it in times of joy and in times of sorrow. 
>
> Remove from us the delusion of separation, and let us realize that Thou art the only Reality. May we see Thee in the eyes of all, and may our lives be a sweet fragrance of Thy peace, Thy joy, and Thy unconditional love to all souls."

*Jai Guru. Jai Ma.*
